sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā ghorarūpāṃ viśāṃ pate dvidhā ciccheda te putraḥ kṣurapreṇa mahārathaḥ
english: As that dread-shaped spear came hurtling suddenly upon him, O lord of peoples, your son, the great chariot-warrior, clove it in two with a razor-edged arrow.

sanskrit: tāṃ śaktiṃ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā kārṣṇiḥ paramakopanaḥ duryodhanaṃ tribhir bāṇair bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: Seeing the spear fall, the son of Kṛṣṇa, blazing with fury, planted three arrows in Duryodhana's arms and breast.

sanskrit: punaś cainaṃ śarair ghorair ājaghāna stanāntare daśabhir bharataśreṣṭha duryodhanam amarṣaṇam
english: And again, O best of the Bhāratas, he struck the unforgiving Duryodhana between the breasts with ten dreadful arrows.

sanskrit: tad yuddham abhavad ghoraṃ citrarūpaṃ ca bhārata īkṣitṛprītijananaṃ sarvapārthivapūjitam
english: That combat grew terrible and wondrous to behold, O Bhārata, a joy to the onlookers and honored by all the kings.

sanskrit: bhīṣmasya nidhanārthāya pārthasya vijayāya ca yuyudhāte raṇe vīrau saubhadrakurupuṃgavau
english: For the slaying of Bhīṣma and for Pārtha's victory the two heroes fought in battle — the son of Subhadrā and the bull among the Kurus.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ rabhasaṃ yuddhe drauṇir brāhmaṇapuṃgavaḥ ājaghānorasi kruddho nārācena paraṃtapaḥ
english: The son of Droṇa, that bull among brāhmaṇas, scorcher of foes, in his wrath struck the impetuous Sātyaki upon the breast with an iron shaft.

sanskrit: śaineyo 'pi guroḥ putraṃ sarvamarmasu bhārata atāḍayad ameyātmā navabhiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: The grandson of Śini too, O Bhārata, that warrior of measureless spirit, smote the teacher's son in all his vital parts with nine heron-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tu samare sātyakiṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ triṃśatā ca punas tūrṇaṃ bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: Aśvatthāman in the battle struck Sātyaki with nine arrows, and then swiftly with thirty more in the arms and breast.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāso droṇaputreṇa sātvataḥ droṇaputraṃ tribhir bāṇair ājaghāna mahāyaśāḥ
english: Deeply pierced by the son of Droṇa, that mighty archer of the Sātvata line, of great renown, struck the son of Droṇa with three arrows.

sanskrit: pauravo dhṛṣṭaketuṃ ca śarair āsādya saṃyuge bahudhā dārayāṃ cakre maheṣvāsaṃ mahāratham
english: Paurava, closing in battle upon Dhṛṣṭaketu, that mighty archer and great chariot-warrior, tore him in many places with his arrows.

sanskrit: tathaiva pauravaṃ yuddhe dhṛṣṭaketur mahārathaḥ triṃśatā niśitair bāṇair vivyādha sumahābalaḥ
english: In the same way Dhṛṣṭaketu, the great chariot-warrior of vast strength, pierced Paurava in the fight with thirty sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: pauravas tu dhanuś chittvā dhṛṣṭaketor mahārathaḥ nanāda balavan nādaṃ vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But Paurava, the great chariot-warrior, having cut Dhṛṣṭaketu's bow, roared a mighty roar and pierced him with ten arrows.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya pauravaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghāna mahārāja trisaptatyā śilīmukhaiḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, he struck Paurava with sharpened arrows, O great king, with seventy-three keen shafts.

sanskrit: tau tu tatra maheṣvāsau mahāmātrau mahārathau mahatā śaravarṣeṇa parasparam avarṣatām
english: There those two mighty archers, men of high station, great chariot-warriors, rained upon one another a vast downpour of arrows.

sanskrit: anyonyasya dhanuś chittvā hayān hatvā ca bhārata virathāv asiyuddhāya saṃgatau tau mahārathau
english: Having cut each other's bows and slain each other's horses, O Bhārata, those two great chariot-warriors, now bereft of cars, closed for combat with swords.

sanskrit: ārṣabhe carmaṇī citre śatacandrapariṣkṛte tārakāśatacitrau ca nistriṃśau sumahāprabhau
english: With bull-hide shields, bright and adorned with a hundred moons, and swords gleaming with great brilliance, dappled as with a hundred stars,

sanskrit: pragṛhya vimalau rājaṃs tāv anyonyam abhidrutau vāśitāsaṃgame yattau siṃhāv iva mahāvane
english: grasping their spotless blades, O king, the two rushed upon each other, eager as two lions in a great forest contending for a mate.

sanskrit: maṇḍalāni vicitrāṇi gatapratyāgatāni ca ceratur darśayantau ca prārthayantau parasparam
english: They wheeled in wondrous circlings, advancing and retreating, displaying their art and each seeking out the other's life.

sanskrit: pauravo dhṛṣṭaketuṃ tu śaṅkhadeśe mahāsinā tāḍayām āsa saṃkruddhas tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Paurava, enraged, struck Dhṛṣṭaketu upon the temple with his great sword and cried, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: cedirājo 'pi samare pauravaṃ puruṣarṣabham ājaghāna śitāgreṇa jatrudeśe mahāsinā
english: The king of the Cedis too, in the battle, struck Paurava, that bull among men, upon the collarbone with the sharp edge of his great sword.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ mahārāja samāsādya mahāhave anyonyavegābhihatau nipetatur ariṃdamau
english: Those two subduers of foes, O great king, having closed with one another in that mighty fray, struck down by each other's onset, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ svaratham āropya pauravaṃ tanayas tava jayatseno rathe rājann apovāha raṇājirāt
english: Then your son Jayatsena, lifting Paurava onto his own chariot, O king, bore him away from the field of battle.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuṃ ca samare mādrīputraḥ paraṃtapaḥ apovāha raṇe rājan sahadevaḥ pratāpavān
english: And Dhṛṣṭaketu, in the fight, the son of Mādrī, the scorcher of foes, valiant Sahadeva, bore away from the battle, O king.

sanskrit: citrasenaḥ suśarmāṇaṃ viddhvā navabhir āśugaiḥ punar vivyādha taṃ ṣaṣṭyā punaś ca navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Citrasena, having pierced Suśarman with nine swift shafts, pierced him again with sixty, and yet again with nine arrows.

sanskrit: suśarmā tu raṇe kruddhas tava putraṃ viśāṃ pate daśabhir daśabhiś caiva vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But Suśarman, enraged in the battle, O lord of peoples, pierced your son with ten and ten sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: citrasenaś ca taṃ rājaṃs triṃśatā nataparvaṇām ājaghāna raṇe kruddhaḥ sa ca taṃ pratyavidhyata bhīṣmasya samare rājan yaśo mānaṃ ca vardhayan
english: And Citrasena, O king, in his wrath struck him in battle with thirty smooth-jointed arrows, and the other pierced him in return, O king, exalting in that fight the glory and honor of Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: saubhadro rājaputraṃ tu bṛhadbalam ayodhayat ārjuniṃ kosalendras tu viddhvā pañcabhir āyasaiḥ punar vivyādha viṃśatyā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: The son of Subhadrā fought with the prince Bṛhadbala; and the lord of Kosala, having pierced the son of Arjuna with five iron shafts, pierced him again with twenty smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: bṛhadbalaṃ ca saubhadro viddhvā navabhir āyasaiḥ nākampayata saṃgrāme vivyādha ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: And the son of Subhadrā, having pierced Bṛhadbala with nine iron shafts, could not make him waver in the battle, yet pierced him again and again.

sanskrit: kausalyasya punaś cāpi dhanuś ciccheda phālguṇiḥ ājaghāna śaraiś caiva triṃśatā kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: And the son of Phalguna once more cut the bow of the prince of Kosala and struck him with thirty heron-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya rājaputro bṛhadbalaḥ phālguniṃ samare kruddho vivyādha bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, the prince Bṛhadbala, enraged, pierced the son of Phalguna in battle with many arrows.

sanskrit: tayor yuddhaṃ samabhavad bhīṣmahetoḥ paraṃtapa saṃrabdhayor mahārāja samare citrayodhinoḥ yathā devāsure yuddhe mayavāsavayor abhūt
english: A combat arose between those two for Bhīṣma's sake, O scorcher of foes — between the two enraged and wondrous fighters in that battle, O great king — even as once in the war of gods and demons between Maya and Vāsava.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno gajānīkaṃ yodhayan bahv aśobhata yathā śakro vajrapāṇir dārayan parvatottamān
english: Bhīmasena shone resplendent as he fought the host of elephants, like Śakra with thunderbolt in hand cleaving the loftiest mountains.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā bhīmena mātaṅgā girisaṃnibhāḥ nipetur urvyāṃ sahitā nādayanto vasuṃdharām
english: Those elephants, huge as hills, slaughtered by Bhīma, fell together to the earth, making the ground resound.

sanskrit: girimātrā hi te nāgā bhinnāñjanacayopamāḥ virejur vasudhāṃ prāpya vikīrṇā iva parvatāḥ
english: Those elephants, vast as mountains and dark as heaps of broken collyrium, lay shining upon the earth, scattered like sundered hills.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro maheṣvāso madrarājānam āhave mahatyā senayā guptaṃ pīḍayām āsa saṃgataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, the mighty archer, closing in battle upon the king of the Madras, who was guarded by a great host, pressed him hard.

sanskrit: madreśvaraś ca samare dharmaputraṃ mahāratham pīḍayām āsa saṃrabdho bhīṣmahetoḥ parākramī
english: And the lord of the Madras, valiant for Bhīṣma's sake, enraged in the battle, pressed hard the son of Dharma, that great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: virāṭaṃ saindhavo rājā viddhvā saṃnataparvabhiḥ navabhiḥ sāyakais tīkṣṇais triṃśatā punar ardayat
english: The king of the Sindhus, having pierced Virāṭa with nine smooth-jointed, sharp shafts, tormented him again with thirty more.

sanskrit: virāṭaś ca mahārāja saindhavaṃ vāhinīmukhe triṃśatā niśitair bāṇair ājaghāna stanāntare
english: And Virāṭa, O great king, at the head of the host struck the king of the Sindhus with thirty sharpened arrows between the breasts.

sanskrit: citrakārmukanistriṃśau citravarmāyudhadhvajau rejatuś citrarūpau tau saṃgrāme matsyasaindhavau
english: With bright bows and swords, with gleaming armor, weapons, and banners, those two of wondrous aspect — the Matsya and the Saindhava — shone resplendent in the battle.

sanskrit: droṇaḥ pāñcālaputreṇa samāgamya mahāraṇe mahāsamudayaṃ cakre śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Droṇa, meeting the son of the Pāñcāla in that great battle, made a vast tumult with his smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tato droṇo mahārāja pārṣatasya mahad dhanuḥ chittvā pañcāśateṣūṇāṃ pārṣataṃ samavidhyata
english: Then Droṇa, O great king, having cut the great bow of the grandson of Pṛṣata, pierced the grandson of Pṛṣata with fifty shafts.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya pārṣataḥ paravīrahā droṇasya miṣato yuddhe preṣayām āsa sāyakān
english: Taking up another bow, the grandson of Pṛṣata, slayer of hostile heroes, loosed his shafts in the fight before Droṇa's very eyes.

sanskrit: tāñ śarāñ śarasaṃghais tu saṃnivārya mahārathaḥ droṇo drupadaputrāya prāhiṇot pañca sāyakān
english: Warding off those arrows with a multitude of his own, the great chariot-warrior Droṇa sent five shafts against the son of Drupada.

sanskrit: tasya kruddho mahārāja pārṣataḥ paravīrahā droṇāya cikṣepa gadāṃ yamadaṇḍopamāṃ raṇe
english: At this, enraged, O great king, the grandson of Pṛṣata, slayer of hostile heroes, hurled at Droṇa in battle a mace like the rod of Yama.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā hemapaṭṭavibhūṣitām śaraiḥ pañcāśatā droṇo vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: As that mace, adorned with bands of gold, came hurtling suddenly upon him, Droṇa warded it off in the fight with fifty arrows.

sanskrit: sā chinnā bahudhā rājan droṇacāpacyutaiḥ śaraiḥ cūrṇīkṛtā viśīryantī papāta vasudhātale
english: Severed in many pieces, O king, by the arrows loosed from Droṇa's bow, that mace, shattered and crumbling, fell to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: gadāṃ vinihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā pārṣataḥ śatrusūdanaḥ droṇāya śaktiṃ cikṣepa sarvapāraśavīṃ śubhām
english: Seeing his mace destroyed, the grandson of Pṛṣata, that slayer of foes, hurled at Droṇa a fair spear wholly wrought of steel.

sanskrit: tāṃ droṇo navabhir bāṇaiś ciccheda yudhi bhārata pārṣataṃ ca maheṣvāsaṃ pīḍayām āsa saṃyuge
english: That spear Droṇa clove with nine arrows in the fight, O Bhārata, and pressed hard in the combat the grandson of Pṛṣata, that mighty archer.

sanskrit: evam etan mahad yuddhaṃ droṇapārṣatayor abhūt bhīṣmaṃ prati mahārāja ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam
english: Thus did this great combat take place between Droṇa and the grandson of Pṛṣata, for Bhīṣma's sake, O great king — dreadful of aspect and terrifying.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ prāpya gāṅgeyaṃ pīḍayan niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ abhyadravata saṃyattaṃ vane mattam iva dvipam
english: Arjuna, reaching the son of Gaṅgā and pressing him with sharpened arrows, rushed upon him as he stood ready, like a hunter upon a rutting elephant in the forest.

sanskrit: pratyudyayau ca taṃ pārthaṃ bhagadattaḥ pratāpavān tridhā bhinnena nāgena madāndhena mahābalaḥ
english: And valiant Bhagadatta, of mighty strength, came forth against that Pārtha upon an elephant whose temples were split in three, blind with rut.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā mahendragajasaṃnibham paraṃ yatnaṃ samāsthāya bībhatsuḥ pratyapadyata
english: As that elephant, like the elephant of great Indra, came hurtling suddenly upon him, Bībhatsu, putting forth his utmost effort, met the charge.

sanskrit: tato gajagato rājā bhagadattaḥ pratāpavān arjunaṃ śaravarṣeṇa vārayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Then king Bhagadatta the valiant, mounted upon his elephant, checked Arjuna in the fight with a downpour of arrows.

sanskrit: arjunas tu raṇe nāgam āyāntaṃ rajatopamam vimalair āyasais tīkṣṇair avidhyata mahāraṇe
english: But Arjuna, in the great battle, pierced that oncoming elephant, white as silver, with spotless, sharp iron shafts.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ ca kaunteyo yāhi yāhīty acodayat bhīṣmaṃ prati mahārāja jahy enam iti cābravīt
english: And the son of Kuntī urged Śikhaṇḍin on, crying "Go! Go!" — "Toward Bhīṣma, O great king — slay him!" he said.

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣas tato hitvā pāṇḍavaṃ pāṇḍupūrvaja prayayau tvarito rājan drupadasya rathaṃ prati
english: Then the lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, O elder of the Pāṇḍu line, leaving the son of Pāṇḍu, hastened, O king, toward the chariot of Drupada.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno mahārāja bhīṣmam abhyadravad drutam śikhaṇḍinaṃ puraskṛtya tato yuddham avartata
english: Then Arjuna, O great king, rushed swiftly upon Bhīṣma, placing Śikhaṇḍin before him, and thereupon the battle was joined.

sanskrit: tatas te tāvakāḥ śūrāḥ pāṇḍavaṃ rabhasaṃ raṇe sarve 'bhyadhāvan krośantas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then those heroes of your side all rushed shouting upon the impetuous son of Pāṇḍu in the battle, and that was a marvelous sight.

sanskrit: nānāvidhāny anīkāni putrāṇāṃ te janādhipa arjuno vyadhamat kāle divīvābhrāṇi mārutaḥ
english: The manifold ranks of your sons, O ruler of men, Arjuna scattered in due season, as the wind scatters the clouds in the sky.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu samāsādya bharatānāṃ pitāmaham iṣubhis tūrṇam avyagro bahubhiḥ sa samācinot
english: But Śikhaṇḍin, closing upon the grandsire of the Bhāratas, unflustered, swiftly covered him over with many arrows.

sanskrit: somakāṃś ca raṇe bhīṣmo jaghne pārthapadānugān nyavārayata sainyaṃ ca pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathaḥ
english: And Bhīṣma in the battle slew the Somakas who followed in Pārtha's train, and the great chariot-warrior held back the army of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: rathāgnyagāraś cāpārcir asiśaktigadendhanaḥ śarasaṃghamahājvālaḥ kṣatriyān samare 'dahat
english: His chariot a fire-altar, his bow its flame, his swords and spears and maces its fuel, and his showers of arrows its great blaze, Bhīṣma consumed the warriors in the battle.

sanskrit: yathā hi sumahān agniḥ kakṣe carati sānilaḥ tathā jajvāla bhīṣmo 'pi divyāny astrāṇy udīrayan
english: As a vast fire, wind-fanned, ranges through the dry brushwood, so too did Bhīṣma blaze, launching his celestial weapons.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṅkhair iṣubhiḥ śitaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ nādayan sa diśo bhīṣmaḥ pradiśaś ca mahāyaśāḥ
english: With gold-feathered arrows, sharpened and smooth-jointed, Bhīṣma of great renown made the quarters and the intermediate quarters resound.

sanskrit: pātayan rathino rājan gajāṃś ca saha sādibhiḥ muṇḍatālavanānīva cakāra sa rathavrajān
english: Striking down the chariot-warriors, O king, and the elephants together with their riders, he made the throngs of chariots like groves of headless palm-trees.

sanskrit: nirmanuṣyān rathān rājan gajān aśvāṃś ca saṃyuge cakāra sa tadā bhīṣmaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Bhīṣma, the foremost of all who bear arms, made the chariots, the elephants, and the horses void of men in that fight, O king.

sanskrit: tasya jyātalanirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ niśamya sarvato rājan samakampanta sainikāḥ
english: Hearing the twang of his bowstring and the slap of his palm-guard, like the crashing of a thunderbolt, the soldiers trembled on every side, O king.

sanskrit: amoghā hy apatan bāṇāḥ pitus te manujeśvara nāsajjanta śarīreṣu bhīṣmacāpacyutāḥ śarāḥ
english: Unerring fell the arrows of your father, O lord of men; the shafts loosed from Bhīṣma's bow did not lodge but passed clean through the bodies.

sanskrit: nirmanuṣyān rathān rājan suyuktāñ javanair hayaiḥ vātāyamānān paśyāma hriyamāṇān viśāṃ pate
english: We beheld chariots void of men, O king, well-yoked with swift horses, carried off like the wind, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: cedikāśikarūṣāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa mahārathāḥ samākhyātāḥ kulaputrās tanutyajaḥ
english: Fourteen thousand warriors of the Cedis, Kāśis, and Karūṣas — renowned great chariot-warriors, men of noble birth, ready to lay down their lives —

sanskrit: aparāvartinaḥ śūrāḥ suvarṇavikṛtadhvajāḥ saṃgrāme bhīṣmam āsādya savājirathakuñjarāḥ jagmus te paralokāya vyāditāsyam ivāntakam
english: those heroes who never turned back, with banners wrought of gold, on closing with Bhīṣma in battle, together with their horses, chariots, and elephants, went to the other world, as though to Death with gaping mouth.

sanskrit: na tatrāsīn mahārāja somakānāṃ mahārathaḥ yaḥ saṃprāpya raṇe bhīṣmaṃ jīvite sma mano dadhe
english: There was not there, O great king, a single great chariot-warrior of the Somakas who, having reached Bhīṣma in the battle, kept his mind set upon living.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca sarvān raṇe yodhān pretarājapuraṃ prati nītān amanyanta janā dṛṣṭvā bhīṣmasya vikramam
english: Beholding the prowess of Bhīṣma, men deemed all those warriors in the battle led away to the city of the king of the dead.

sanskrit: na kaś cid enaṃ samare pratyudyāti mahārathaḥ ṛte pāṇḍusutaṃ vīraṃ śvetāśvaṃ kṛṣṇasārathim śikhaṇḍinaṃ ca samare pāñcālyam amitaujasam
english: No great chariot-warrior went forth against him in the battle, save the heroic son of Pāṇḍu, he of the white steeds and Kṛṣṇa for charioteer, and Śikhaṇḍin the Pāñcāla of measureless might.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu raṇe bhīṣmam āsādya bharatarṣabha daśabhir daśabhir bāṇair ājaghāna mahāhave
english: But Śikhaṇḍin, closing upon Bhīṣma in the battle, O bull of the Bhāratas, struck him in that great fray with arrows by tens and tens.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ tu gāṅgeyaḥ krodhadīptena cakṣuṣā avaikṣata kaṭākṣeṇa nirdahann iva bhārata
english: But the son of Gaṅgā looked upon Śikhaṇḍin with an eye blazing with wrath, with a sidelong glance, as though to burn him up, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: strītvaṃ tat saṃsmaran rājan sarvalokasya paśyataḥ na jaghāna raṇe bhīṣmaḥ sa ca taṃ nāvabuddhavān
english: Remembering his womanhood, O king, in the sight of all the world, Bhīṣma did not strike him in the battle; and Śikhaṇḍin did not perceive this.

sanskrit: arjunas tu mahārāja śikhaṇḍinam abhāṣata abhitvarasva tvarito jahi cainaṃ pitāmaham
english: But Arjuna, O great king, spoke to Śikhaṇḍin: "Make haste, hasten on, and slay this grandsire!

sanskrit: kiṃ te vivakṣayā vīra jahi bhīṣmaṃ mahāratham na hy anyam anupaśyāmi kaṃ cid yaudhiṣṭhire bale
english: What need of speech, O hero? Slay Bhīṣma, that great chariot-warrior. For I see no other in all Yudhiṣṭhira's host

sanskrit: yaḥ śaktaḥ samare bhīṣmaṃ yodhayeta pitāmaham ṛte tvāṃ puruṣavyāghra satyam etad bravīmi te
english: who is able to do battle in the field with Bhīṣma the grandsire, save you, O tiger among men — this truth I tell you."
